0.long_answer: Hereditary neuralgic amyotrophy (HNA) is the neuralgic syndrome that is clinically similar to acute brachial neuritis, also known as Parsonage–Turner syndrome, and is associated with mutations in the SEPT9 gene located at 17q25. HNA is characterized by episodes of severe pain, followed by muscle weakness and atrophy, particularly affecting the upper limbs. About 50% of HNA cases have been linked to a mutation or duplication in the SEPT9 gene, which plays a role in cellular processes and nerve integrity. This genetic association helps distinguish HNA from sporadic cases of brachial neuritis and provides insight into the hereditary nature of the disorder.
